facts.statement: The study used a mouse model of depression caused by corticosterone and a cell culture of hippocampal neurons to test the link between two proteins.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Researchers measured changes in behavior, cell damage, and the structure and function of synapses and mitochondria.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: In mice treated with corticosterone, levels of the protein XBP-1s went up while the protein EAAT2 went down, and glutamate levels rose in the hippocampus.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: When researchers lowered XBP-1 levels in the neuron cells, EAAT2 protein levels returned to normal and excess glutamate and oxidative stress decreased.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: Giving mice a drug called Toyocamycin lessened depression-like symptoms and brain cell damage, which matched with lower XBP-1s and higher EAAT2 levels.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The results suggest that the activity of XBP-1 signaling is functionally linked to how much EAAT2 is expressed in these specific experimental setups.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The authors state that it is still unknown if EAAT2 is the specific reason why lowering XBP-1 protects the neurons.
facts.subject: animals
